answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to lock a scarce token in a publicly auditable stake contract before it can submit jobs or earn fees. The contract releases the stake only after a waiting period and lets peers slash it for provable double-spending or fabricated attestations. One umber account may look harmless, but multiplying identities means buying and immobilizing real capital; a ripple of coordinated fraud risks forfeiting that stake, while the tide of cheap disposable accounts loses its advantage.
